errors.english: Therefore, it is incorrect for space to have the nature of being space
errors.why: The clause completes the previous side: qualities such as pervasiveness, being other than the substance, cannot be the nature of space; it is not about space having the nature of space.

fix.find: Therefore, it is incorrect for space to have the nature of being space
fix.replace: This is because qualities such as pervasiveness, being things other than the substance, cannot be the nature of space

errors.english: possessing a number is also impossible, because those two [note: number and collection/inherence]
errors.why: གྲངས་དང་ལྡན་པ are the two Vaiśeṣika qualities number (saṃkhyā) and conjunction (saṃyoga), which reside only in substances; not 'possessing a number', and not collection or inherence.

fix.find: possessing a number is also impossible, because those two [note: number and collection/inherence]
fix.replace: number and conjunction are also impossible, because those two [note: number (saṃkhyā) and conjunction (saṃyoga)]

errors.english: because it is unreasonable for the essence of one entity to be entirely distinct and separate from another entity
errors.why: The point is that it is unreasonable for the nature of one thing to be a different thing (a nature separate from its bearer), not that one entity's essence cannot differ from another entity.

note: The regress argument and the six-categories passage are followed well, but the opening clause is misconstrued and number/conjunction is mistranslated.

errors.english: he led them to settle
errors.why: གནས་འཆའ་བ is the Vinaya act of taking dependence (niśraya): Udāyin had them take dependence on himself.

fix.replace: he had them take dependence (niśraya) on him

errors.english: Except for the plants that do not grow
errors.why: With སྲོགས་ཆགས་ ending the previous side, the exception is grass in which living creatures do not breed, not 'plants that do not grow'.

errors.english: bundles of grass should be spread out, bound with ropes, and hung from trees to be kept
errors.why: The bundles meant for spreading on the path are to be tied and hung in trees until use; they are not to be spread out.

errors.english: The clay materials used for cleaning should be placed in earthenware shards
errors.why: The plastering material named is cow dung (ལྕི་བ), which the English drops in favour of 'clay'.

note: The eviction-offence narrative reads well, but the niśraya term and several details of the walking-path rules are wrong.

errors.english: possess an essence of diligence because the benefit of beings is never exhausted
errors.why: The verse says they are by nature diligent in ending what harms beings (ཕན་མིན་ཟད་ཕྱིར), not that beings' benefit is never exhausted.

fix.find: possess an essence of diligence because the benefit of beings is never exhausted
fix.replace: are by nature diligent in putting an end to what harms beings

errors.english: finders of the elements [note: essential qualities] like yourselves are not easily found
errors.why: འབྱུང་བ here is the appearance or birth of beings like you, which is rare; it has nothing to do with 'elements'.

fix.find: finders of the elements [note: essential qualities] like yourselves are not easily found
fix.replace: the appearance of ones like yourselves is not easily found

errors.english: The wisdom that arises toward them
errors.why: The verse says that the person in whom this understanding arises is the one who serves them (the parents); it is not the wisdom that depends on them.

errors.english: he was like the Lord of the Immortals [note: Indra] or the Preceptor of the Gods [note: Brihaspati]
errors.why: The compound names one figure, the guru of the gods of the lord of the immortals (Bṛhaspati, Indra's preceptor), not two alternatives.

errors.english: (Smriti) mindfulness/scripture
errors.why: Paired with the Vedas, smṛti here is the body of traditional law texts (dharmaśāstra); 'mindfulness' is misleading.

note: The prose frame is serviceable, but several verses are misparsed, and inline glosses clutter the text.

errors.english: Who considers that this is not of the same nature as reality? It is by all those who do not perceive the supreme.
errors.why: The root text says reality is not accessible to all who do not see the highest; the commentary then asks 'to whom?', not who holds a view.

note: Sound overall; the root-verse lemma at the start is garbled, but the argument about the elephant's gaze is rendered well.

errors.english: Like another refers to a comparison made through analogy.
errors.why: These are two separate glosses: 'of another' means of someone else, and 'like' means comparison by analogy; the first is lost.

note: A faithful rendering of the word-by-word commentary on the tigress episode, with one merged gloss.

errors.english: Who is the actual builder in relation to this offense?
errors.why: བྱེད་པ་པོ here is the operative factor that constitutes the offence (the vihāra being built), not a 'builder'; the misreading recurs throughout the side.

errors.english: just as one currently speaks of owning a house
errors.why: The point is that, unlike the earlier rule, the qualifier 'having an owner' (as for a house) is not specified here, so the rule covers any vihāra; it is not an analogy with speaking of owning a house.

note: The question-and-answer structure is kept, but the key Vinaya term བྱེད་པ་པོ is systematically rendered as 'builder'.

errors.english: connecting with the cognitive object
errors.why: དམིགས་པ is the verb 'is observed' (ཉེ་བར་དམིགས་སོ in the next sentence) with which 'from which [indicating] cause' is construed, not 'the cognitive object'.

errors.english: Even if any particular distinction among wind and the other humors is indeed a cause
errors.why: The whole passage from གལ་ཏེ through ལྷན་ཅིག་བྱེད་པ་ཅན་ཡིན་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ is the anticipated objection introduced by 'or if the effect'; the English presents most of it as the author's own assertion.

errors.english: the objection is raised: "It is not so..."
errors.why: 'It is not so' rejects the doubt (དོགས་པ་ ... འགོག་པའོ); the English makes it the raising of an objection.

note: Follows a dense lemma-commentary reasonably, but misreads one construal and blurs where the opponent's objection begins and ends.

errors.english: It is because one intends to communicate in such a way
errors.why: བརྡ་བྱེད་པ is the maker of the convention (the mantra's author, as glossed on the previous side), whose intention fixes the result; it is not 'one' intending to communicate.

errors.english: by transforming the mental continuum [note: original: (saṃtāna) the stream of consciousness]
errors.why: The continuum is that of the produced mantra, which is transformed by successive distinctions; it is not the practitioner's stream of consciousness.

errors.english: rather, the mantras are unmanifest
errors.why: The clause is about the application (it does not produce mantras, nor does it manifest them), not a claim that the mantras are unmanifest.

note: The anti-Mīmāṃsā argument on mantra efficacy is largely clear, with a few misconstrued clauses.

errors.english: are worthy of worship even by spiritual teachers for wise men
errors.why: The verse says parents are worthy of worship even by the teachers of the wise (cf. Skt. gurūṇām api); 'for wise men' misattaches མཁས་རྣམས་ཀྱི.

note: The bilingual verses are translated faithfully from the Tibetan, with Sanskrit renderings in notes; one phrase is misattached.
An accurate verse rendering of the argument for the single-characteristic reason (anyathānupapatti) against the triple mark.
